title: How do these five families of shapes overlap?
description: A Venn diagram of five families is drawn and three questions are answered by testing the rules of the families. A kite that is also a parallelogram has four equal sides, a kite that is also a rectangle is a square, and a kite with sides six, six, nine and nine is not a rhombus.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shape sits in the overlap of two families when it meets both rules. Watch for students who think that because every rhombus is a kite, every kite is a rhombus.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 4)
video_script.why: The child tests shapes against the rules of the families, as in the solved example, to place five families in a Venn diagram and answer three questions.
video_script.substitution: the book's own five families: parallelograms, kites, rhombuses, rectangles and squares
video_script.anchor: a Venn diagram of parallelograms, kites, rhombuses, rectangles and squares
video_script.payoff_line: The shape that is both a kite and a parallelogram is a rhombus

final_answer.value: (i) A rhombus; (ii) Yes, a square; (iii) No; every rhombus is a kite, but not every kite is a rhombus
final_answer.spoken: first a rhombus, second yes a square, and third no, every rhombus is a kite but not every kite is a rhombus

hold_back: (i) A rhombus; (ii) Yes, a square; (iii) No; every rhombus is a kite, but not every kite is a rhombus
never_show: a kite with sides 6, 6, 9, 9 named a rhombus
maths_rules: parallelograms hold rectangles and rhombuses, and squares are in their overlap
a kite and a parallelogram together have opposite sides equal and neighbouring sides equal in pairs, so all four sides are equal: a rhombus (squares included)
a rectangle is a parallelogram with all angles 90; a kite that is a rectangle has four equal sides and four right angles, so it is a square
a kite can have sides 6, 6, 9 and 9, whose sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus
a rhombus has neighbouring sides equal in pairs, so every rhombus is a kite

<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of these families overlap?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

<bookmark mark='hoop'/>A shape sits in a hoop when it meets the rule of that family.

beats.on_screen: Given: five families. Questions: (i) both a kite and a parallelogram? (ii) both a kite and a rectangle? (iii) is every kite a rhombus?
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, parallelograms, kites, rhombuses, rectangles and squares.
<bookmark mark='qs'/>We answer three questions about them.

beats.on_screen: To find: the Venn diagram and the answers to the three questions

beats.on_screen: Step 1: parallelograms hold rectangles and rhombuses; squares sit in their overlap; the kite hoop overlaps the parallelogram hoop

marks.draw: the rectangle hoop and the rhombus hoop are drawn inside the parallelogram hoop
marks.sq: the square sits where those two hoops overlap
marks.kite: the kite hoop is drawn across the edge of the parallelogram hoop

narration: <bookmark mark='draw'/>Step one, draw rectangles and rhombuses inside the parallelograms.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>Squares sit where the rectangles and rhombuses overlap.
<bookmark mark='kite'/>The kites overlap the parallelograms, and the next step shows exactly where.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: (i) a kite that is a parallelogram: neighbouring sides equal in a kite, opposite sides equal in a parallelogram, so all four sides are equal

marks.kite: two neighbouring sides are ticked equal
marks.par: each side is ticked equal to its opposite
marks.all: all four sides are ticked equal

narration: <bookmark mark='kite'/>Step two, in a kite, two neighbouring sides are equal.
<bookmark mark='par'/>In a parallelogram, each side equals its opposite side.
<bookmark mark='all'/>A shape with both rules has all four sides equal, which is a rhombus.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: (ii) a rectangle is a parallelogram with all angles 90°; if it is also a kite, all four sides are equal, so it is a square

marks.rect: a rectangle is shown with four right angles
marks.eq: all four sides are ticked equal as in the last step

narration: <bookmark mark='rect'/>Step three, a rectangle is a parallelogram with all angles ninety degrees.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>If it is also a kite, all four sides are equal, as in step two.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>Four equal sides and four right angles make a square.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: (iii) a kite with sides 6, 6, 9 and 9 is not a rhombus; a rhombus has neighbouring sides equal in pairs, so it is a kite

marks.kite: a kite with sides six, six, nine and nine is drawn
marks.no: the word rhombus is crossed out beside it
marks.rev: a rhombus is drawn inside the kite hoop

narration: <bookmark mark='kite'/>Step four, a kite can have sides six, six, nine and nine.
<bookmark mark='no'/>Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus.
<bookmark mark='rev'/>A rhombus has all sides equal, so it is a kite.
But a kite need not be a rhombus.

beats.on_screen: Check: the kite with sides 6, 6, 9, 9 sits in the kite hoop outside the rhombus hoop; every rhombus sits inside the kite hoop

marks.out: the kite with sides six, six, nine and nine glows outside the rhombus hoop

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, check the finished diagram.
<bookmark mark='out'/>The kite with sides six, six, nine and nine sits outside the rhombus hoop.
<bookmark mark='in'/>The rhombus hoop sits inside the kite hoop.
To test an every statement, one shape that breaks it is enough.
